label: thm:ftc2
title: Second Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
statement:
Let $F : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$ and have right derivative $f'(x)$ at every $x \in (\min(a,b), \max(a,b))$, i.e., $\texttt{HasDerivWithinAt}\; F\; (f'\; x)\; (x, +\infty)\; x$. If $f'$ is interval integrable on $[a,b]$, then
    \[
      \int_a^b f'(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a).
    \]
    In Mathlib this is \texttt{intervalIntegral.integral\_eq\_sub\_of\_hasDeriv\_right}.
proof: Direct application of \texttt{intervalIntegral.integral\_eq\_sub\_of\_hasDeriv\_right}, given the continuity of $F$ on $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$, the right-derivative hypothesis on the interior, and the integrability of $f'$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:continuous_integrable}).
